newsitem.title: UK: Australian Aboriginal asks UK for ancestor's head.
newsitem.headline: Australian Aboriginal asks UK for ancestor's head.

text.p: An Australian Aboriginal leader arrives in Britain on Tuesday to fight for the return of the severed head of an Aboriginal hero which lies buried among other corpses in an unmarked grave in northern England.

The head of 19th-century Aboriginal leader Yagan was hacked from his body after his murder in 1833 near Perth and smoked to preserve it. It was later placed in a museum in Liverpool, England, before being buried in 1964.
Aboriginal demands for the head's return have been rejected by the British government because it shares its public grave with the corpses of 20 stillborn babies.
Under British law, their parents would have to give consent before the grave could be disturbed to exhume Yagan's head.

Ken Colbung, a 66-year-old Aboriginal activist and the closest living relative of Yagan, plans to fly to Britain and try to meet government ministers in the hope that the new Labour government, elected on May 1, can help resolve the dispute.
"Two grim histories have been unearthed by the discovery of Yagan's head," Colbung said in a statement on Sunday.

"I have all the sympathy in the world for the families of the babies who rest with Yagan, but he is not yet at rest. I want to meet and talk with the families and explain the importance that my people place in his return home."

Colbung searched for Yagan's head for decades before discovering in 1993 that it had been buried in the Liverpool cemetery. He said that according to Aboriginal beliefs, Yagan's spirit would remain earthbound until his head was reunited with the rest of his remains.

One of the relatives of the dead babies buried above Yagan's head has objected to the grave being disturbed, but Colbung said he hoped the government would override any objections and authorise an exhumation.
"The Labour Party have cut a swathe through government in their first weeks in office," he said. "I hope there is still some energy left in them to resolve this case."
